title: Independent final repairs for three Reading the Landscape slide headings
scope: Read-only heading repairs only. No repository file was changed. Sesotho object-form check consulted a Peace Corps beginner Sesotho tutorial, which uses “li tla u thusa” (“they will help you”); remaining Tshivenda/Xitsonga forms are conservative semantic drafts requiring fluent-speaker review.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Watch: See Wind and Cold Air on the Map
entries.currentCandidate: Shebella: See Wind and Cold Air mapa
entries.repairedCandidate: Shebella: See Wind and Cold Air on the Map
entries.independentFinding: “mapa” names a map but the candidate does not clearly express the source relation “on the map.” Keep the locative phrase exact in English until a reviewed Sesotho form is available.
entries.repairRationale: Conservative restoration of the exact source prepositional relation.
entries.reviewStatus: unreviewed machine draft; target-language fluency and local approval not claimed

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Let Plants Help You Read Soil
entries.currentCandidate: Lumella dimela di go thuse ho bala Soil
entries.repairedCandidate: Lumella dimela di u thuse ho bala Soil
entries.independentFinding: “go” is the object form commonly associated with Northern Sotho/Sepedi, while Southern Sesotho uses “u” for the second-person object in examples such as “li tla u thusa” (“they will help you”). “di u thuse” keeps plants as the subject and you as object in the directive construction.
entries.repairRationale: Change go to u; retain the candidate’s “Let plants help you read Soil” construction. This is a conservative grammar correction, not a fluent approval.
entries.reviewStatus: unreviewed machine draft; target-language fluency and local approval not claimed

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Let Plants Help You Read Soil
entries.currentCandidate: Zwilimela zwi nga ni thusa u vhala Soil
entries.repairedCandidate: Tendelani zwilimela zwi ni thuse u read Soil
entries.independentFinding: Current “Zwilimela zwi nga ni thusa...” back-translates as “Plants can help you...,” shifting the source directive “Let plants help you...” to a possibility statement. The repair uses a directive “allow/let plants...” construction and leaves the difficult technical phrase “read Soil” in English.
entries.repairRationale: Proposed directive form for facilitator review; preserve Read Soil as exact English anchor.
entries.reviewStatus: unreviewed machine draft; target-language fluency and local approval not claimed
